text:
sara: Heads up — nodepool `us-east1-gpu-2` failed provisioning, ALB healthchecks keep timing out and nodes stay in NotReady. Seen about ~6 failed instances in last 10m. Logs: `kubectl describe node` shows kubelet failing to reach API on certain ephemeral ports.

oncall-bot: [alert] nodepool-us-east1-gpu-2: 6/6 failing health checks — incident created #INC-4821

tom: Any recent network stuffs? NACL/SG changes rolled out in the last hour?

devon: I pushed a tiny NACL hardening for a subset of subnets earlier (nacl-hardening-2026) but I thought it targeted only staging subnets. Didn’t touch prod ASGs. I’ll double-check.

sara: I tried `curl http://<node-ip>:10256/healthz` from the bastion and it times out. Traceroute stops at the NAT gw: `traceroute to <node-ip> (10.x.x.x), 30 hops max ... 8  nat-gw-1 (10.x.x.1) * * *`

devon: That suggests egress or ephemeral port return path is blocked. Quick check — can you run `aws ec2 describe-network-acls --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-abc123 --query 'NetworkAcls[*].Entries'` and paste the relevant rules? I’ll look for a deny on high ports.

sara: Paste from the subnet's NACL: ```
RuleNumber: 100
Protocol: 6 (TCP)
RuleAction: deny
Egress: false
CidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0
PortRange: 32768-65535
```

tom: Oof. That blocks ephemeral ports inbound which breaks responses to ALB health checks (ALB uses ephemeral source ports for health checks and nodes respond back).

devon: Ugh — looks like the NACL was intended for a different private subnet. Investigating ASG subnets... `aws autoscaling describe-auto-scaling-groups --auto-scaling-group-names asg-us-east-gpu-2 --query 'AutoScalingGroups[*].VPCZoneIdentifier'` shows `subnet-aaa,subnet-bbb` and subnet-bbb is the one I hardened by mistake. The ASG is launching into the hardened subnet.

sara: That explains it. So two action paths: 1) quick mitigation: allow ephemeral ports back on that NACL so healthchecks/established flows work OR 2) move ASG to the correct subnet and roll forward terraform fix. Which do we want for immediate recovery?

tom: Immediate = ephemeral allow. We can tighten it after we move ASG. Also add a temporary security group rule to allow ALB SG -> node SG on TCP ephemeral range.

devon: Applying quick NACL patch now and will open a terraform PR to correct ASG subnet mapping + add unit test to prevent subnet mismatch. CLI I’m running: ```bash
aws ec2 replace-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id acl-0abc --rule-number 100 --protocol 6 --rule-action allow --egress false --cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --port-range From=32768,To=65535
```

devon: Patch applied. Also added SG rule: `allow tcp 32768-65535 from sg-alb` on node SG.

sara: Confirmed — ALB healthchecks passing, nodes registered back into cluster. Kube nodes moved to Ready within 2mins. :thumbsup:

devon: Opening PR #4321 to: 1) update ASG subnets to `subnet-correct-1,subnet-correct-2`, 2) add terraform guardrail that fails plan if ASG references hardened subnet tag `nacl-strict=true`, 3) add small e2e that exercises ALB->node healthcheck path. Link: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pull/4321

tom: After PR merges, we should remove the broad ephemeral allow and instead explicitly allow only ALB CIDRs if possible. Also add a runbook note that NACL changes require confirming no ASGs use that subnet.

devon: Agreed. Will rollback the broad allow via another PR after ASG fix and add a scheduled scan that flags any ASG-subnet mismatches.

sara: Great — thanks all. Leaving incident open until PR lands and we revert the temp rule.

oncall-bot: Incident #INC-4821 updated: status = mitigated (healthchecks green), owner = devon, next steps = PR #4321, revert ACL after validation.
